name: Minimum-voltage measuring relay
summary: Measuring relay that operates when voltage falls below a set level while some voltage is still present.
description: The minimum-voltage relay form operates when the measured voltage falls below its setting. It is used for motor undervoltage tripping, load shedding and transfer schemes, where a sustained voltage dip indicates a supply problem rather than a momentary disturbance.

The symbol shows the voltage quantity and the less-than threshold but not the time delay, which phases are monitored or whether operation is blocked on VT fuse failure. Without a blocking input a blown VT fuse can cause an unwanted trip, so the supervision arrangement should be cross-referenced.
readingNotes: Check which phase voltages are monitored.
Look for VT supervision or fuse-failure blocking.
distinction: A minimum-voltage relay responds to a reduced voltage; a loss-of-voltage relay responds to absence of voltage.
